knowledge_point.title: Determining the Equation of a Normal Line to a Curve at a Point

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=x^{2} + 2 x$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=2 x + 2
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(2\right)=2 \left(2\right) + 2=6
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(6\right)}=- \frac{1}{6}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(8\right)&=- \frac{1}{6}\left(x-\left(2\right)\right)\\
y&=- \frac{x}{6}+\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)+\left(8\right)\\
y&=\frac{25}{3} - \frac{x}{6}
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $a=- \frac{1}{6}$ and $b=\frac{25}{3}$.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=- \frac{x^{6}}{8} + \frac{7 x^{3}}{4} + 1$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=- \frac{3 x^{5}}{4} + \frac{21 x^{2}}{4}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(2\right)=- \frac{3 \left(2\right)^{5}}{4} + \frac{21 \left(2\right)^{2}}{4}=-3
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(-3\right)}=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(7\right)&=\frac{1}{3}\left(x-\left(2\right)\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{3}+\left(- \frac{2}{3}\right)+\left(7\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{3} + \frac{19}{3}\\
\left(-3\right)y&=-x+\left(2\right)+\left(-21\right)\\
x+\left(-3\right)y&=-19
\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient is $-3$ and the constant is $-19$.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=2 x^{3} + 2 x + 2$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=6 x^{2} + 2
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(1\right)=6 \left(1\right)^{2} + 2=8
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(8\right)}=- \frac{1}{8}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(6\right)&=- \frac{1}{8}\left(x-\left(1\right)\right)\\
y&=- \frac{x}{8}+\left(\frac{1}{8}\right)+\left(6\right)\\
y&=\frac{49}{8} - \frac{x}{8}\\
\left(8\right)y&=-x+\left(1\right)+\left(48\right)\\
x+\left(8\right)y&=49
\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient is $8$ and the constant is $49$.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=2 - \frac{2}{x} - \frac{2}{x^{2}}$. Rewrite with powers, then differentiate term by term:

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)&=(-2x^{-1})+(-2x^{-2})+(2)\\
f'(x)&=\frac{2}{x^{2}} + \frac{4}{x^{3}}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(2\right)=\frac{2}{\left(2\right)^{2}} + \frac{4}{\left(2\right)^{3}}=1
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(1\right)}=-1.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)&=-1\left(x-\left(2\right)\right)\\
y&=- x+\left(2\right)+\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\\
y&=\frac{5}{2} - x
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $a=-1$ and $b=\frac{5}{2}$.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=- 2 \sqrt[3]{x} - x - 1$. Rewrite with powers, then differentiate term by term:

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)&=(-2x^{\frac{1}{3}})+(-1x^{1})+(-1)\\
f'(x)&=-1 - \frac{2}{3 x^{\frac{2}{3}}}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(1\right)=-1 - \frac{2}{3 \left(1\right)^{\frac{2}{3}}}=- \frac{5}{3}
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(- \frac{5}{3}\right)}=\frac{3}{5}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-4\right)&=\frac{3}{5}\left(x-\left(1\right)\right)\\
y&=\frac{3 x}{5}+\left(- \frac{3}{5}\right)+\left(-4\right)\\
y&=\frac{3 x}{5} - \frac{23}{5}
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $a=\frac{3}{5}$ and $b=- \frac{23}{5}$.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=\frac{1}{x} + \frac{2}{\sqrt{x}}$. Rewrite with powers, then differentiate term by term:

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)&=(2x^{- \frac{1}{2}})+(1x^{-1})+(0)\\
f'(x)&=- \frac{1}{x^{2}} - \frac{1}{x^{\frac{3}{2}}}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(1\right)=- \frac{1}{\left(1\right)^{2}} - \frac{1}{\left(1\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}}=-2
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(-2\right)}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(3\right)&=\frac{1}{2}\left(x-\left(1\right)\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{2}+\left(- \frac{1}{2}\right)+\left(3\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{2} + \frac{5}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $a=\frac{1}{2}$ and $b=\frac{5}{2}$.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=x^3+x+1$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=3x^2+1.
$$

At $(1,3)$ the tangent slope is $f'(1)=4$, so the normal slope is $-\frac{1}{4}$. Use point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-3&=-\frac{1}{4}(x-1)\\
4y-12&=-x+1\\
x+4y&=13.
\end{aligned}
$$

The first blank is $4$ and the second is $13$.

question.:question/worked-solution:
The tangent slope is

$$
f'(1)=2(1)=2.
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so its slope is

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Use the point $(1,1)$ in point-slope form:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-1&=-\frac{1}{2}(x-1)\\
y&=-\frac{1}{2}x+\frac{3}{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The first blank is $-\frac{1}{2}$ and the second is $\frac{3}{2}$.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=- \frac{x^{6}}{8} + x^{3} - 1$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=- \frac{3 x^{5}}{4} + 3 x^{2}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(2\right)=- \frac{3 \left(2\right)^{5}}{4} + 3 \left(2\right)^{2}=-12
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(-12\right)}=\frac{1}{12}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-1\right)&=\frac{1}{12}\left(x-\left(2\right)\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{12}+\left(- \frac{1}{6}\right)+\left(-1\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{12} - \frac{7}{6}\\
\left(-12\right)y&=-x+\left(2\right)+\left(12\right)\\
x+\left(-12\right)y&=14
\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient is $-12$ and the constant is $14$.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=- x^{2} + x$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=1 - 2 x
$$

$$
m_t=f'\left(2\right)=1 - 2 \left(2\right)=-3
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(-3\right)}=\frac{1}{3}.

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-2\right)&=\frac{1}{3}\left(x-\left(2\right)\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{3}+\left(- \frac{2}{3}\right)+\left(-2\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{3} - \frac{8}{3}\\
\left(-3\right)y&=-x+\left(2\right)+\left(6\right)\\
x+\left(-3\right)y&=8

$$

The coefficient is $-3$ and the constant is $8$.
